This article hits on what I thought was the real story in Ferguson. Local governments are required by Federal laws, State laws, and local resident demands to do certain things. These things cost money. In many communities, there just isn't the tax base and/or residents refuse to raise taxes. The local government officials then turn to (what I think are) excessive fees and fines to make up the difference. Sometimes the fees pay for shiny new equipment and buildings and sometimes it's to just keep the lights on.

I don't have a good answer to resolve this - perhaps give financially stressed communities the ability to prioritize which government mandates they will follow? Perhaps re-write such mandates such that poorer communities have less burden? Otherwise you can't get blood from a stone.

In any event, I see this issue affecting communities across the country, both urban and rural.
Or get rid of the government mandates altogether.
